51572336.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to uPAR H47C/N259C (unknown origin) mutant assessed as equilibrium dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis relative to control

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: To determine the equilibrium binding constants (K_D) of these 29 compounds binding to the stable uPAR variant, uPAR(H47C/N259C), surface plasmon resonance analysis (SPR) was performed on a BIACORE T200 instrument (BIACORE, Uppsala, Sweden). A CMS chip was coupled with uPAR(H47C/N259C) by injecting the protein in a concentration of 30 μg/mL in immobilization buffer (10 mM sodium acetate, pH 5.0), aiming for an immobilized level of approximately 10,000 response units (RUs). Immobilization was followed by surface blocking with ethanolamine. A reference cell was prepared in the same way, without coupling of uPAR(H47C/N259C). Running buffer containing these 29 compounds at a concentration of 100 μM was injected at a flow rate of 30 μL per min for 120 s at 25 °C. Subsequently, the dissociation was monitored for 300 s. The increased RU (delta RU) subtracted from the blank was recorded. Compounds with delta RU > 10 were selected for the determination of K_D values. The determination of K_D values was performed by the above setup while at a concentration range of 0–100 μM. The K_D values were calculated based on the steady-state-affinity modulation.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Experimental validation of uPAR inhibitors. (A) Increases in the SPR RU when uPAR(H47C/N259C) treated with the 29 compounds (100 μM) with highest consensus scores in virtual screening. (B–E) SPR sensorgrams and fitted curves of compounds (B) 4, (C) 5, (D) 22, (E) 26, and (F) 27 binding to uPAR(H47C/N259C). K_D values were calculated according to the fitted curves. (G–H) Determination of the IC_50 values of 22 (G) and 26 (H) inhibiting the uPA–uPAR interaction using an ELISA method. The scheme of the ELISA test is represented in Figure S3. Values are represented as mean ± standard deviation (SD) (N = 3).
original_paragraph.Figure 3B-F: The sensorgrams in Figure 3B–F show the binding response over time (x-axis: Time / s) for compounds 4, 5, 22, 26, and 27 at concentrations of 100, 50, 25, 12.5, and 6.25 μM. The fitted curves are shown below each sensorgram, with the calculated K_D values: K_D = 41.2 ± 13.4 μM for compound 4, K_D = 79.7 ± 6.2 μM for compound 5, K_D = 39.2 ± 8.0 μM for compound 22, K_D = 40.4 ± 2.0 μM for compound 26, and K_D = 113.9 ± 10.6 μM for compound 27.
original_paragraph.Figure 3G-H: The IC_50 values for compounds 22 and 26 are shown in Figure 3G and 3H, respectively. The x-axis represents the concentration of the compound (Concentration / M) on a logarithmic scale. The IC_50 values are reported as: IC_50 = 58.6 ± 6.9 μM for compound 22 and IC_50 = 69.5 ± 10.1 μM for compound 26.
